question_text: Two municipal trucks leave depot in opposite directions: 40 km/h and 50 km/h. When will they be 270 km apart?

hint_ladder.title: Isipin ang Direksyon
hint_ladder.text: Kapag magkasalungat ang galaw, ang bilis nila ay pinagsasama. So 40 + 50 = 90 km/h ang relative speed.

hint_ladder.title: Gamitin ang Distance Formula
hint_ladder.text: Oras = Distansya ÷ Bilis. Dito, 270 km ÷ 90 km/h = 3 oras. Simplehan lang, parang pagbibilang ng oras sa biyahe.

hint_ladder.title: I-check ang Sagot Mo
hint_ladder.text: Sa 3 oras, nakakalayo ng 120 km ang isa, 150 km ang isa. Total 270 km. Tama! Kaya C ang sagot.

hint_ladder.title: Huwag Magulo sa Subtraction
hint_ladder.text: Common mistake: binabawas ang speeds. Sa opposite, addition. Isipin parang layo nila nag-aadd up, hindi nagkakalapit.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you mistakenly used a relative speed of 135 km/h (40+50 doubled?), leading to 270/135=2h.

B.text: You might have chosen B because you divided 270 by the average speed (45 km/h) and then incorrectly halved the result to get 2.5h.

C.text: Correct. When moving in opposite directions, add the speeds (40+50=90 km/h), then divide distance: 270 ÷ 90 = 3 hours.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you subtracted the speeds (50-40=10 km/h) then divided 270 by 10, misplacing the decimal to get 3.5h.

next_time_rule: Kapag magkasalungat, i-add ang speeds; kapag magkasunod, i-subtract. Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed. Dali!
deconstruct_text:
Imagine two LGU delivery trucks from the municipal hall in Tarlac heading to opposite barangays—one to the north at 40 km/h, the other to the south at 50 km/h. Since they go opposite directions, their separation speed adds up: 40 + 50 = 90 km/h.

To find how long until they're 270 km apart, use Time = Distance / Relative Speed. So 270 km divided by 90 km/h gives exactly 3 hours. That's option C.
